name: Koira
description: Koira (Finnish for 'Dog') is a traditional Finnish card game for three to eight players. It is an avoidance game belonging to the 'beating' family (like Skitgubbe). The game is famous for its social element: the loser is called the 'Dog' and may be jokingly required to bark. It is played in two distinct phases: a collection phase where card count is expanded, and an avoidance phase where players try to empty their hands.

history.origins: Originates from 19th-century Finnish folk traditions, closely related to the Swedish game Skitgubbe and the Norwegian Mattis. It was historically a common game among forestry workers and farming families.
timeline: 1800s: Emerges as a folk variation of Northern European beating games.
1950s: Standardized rules appear in Finnish game books.
Present: Remains a popular 'last person loses' social game in Finland.
history.cultural: In Finnish culture, being the 'Koira' is a humorous mark of bad luck in cards.
history.evolution: The game's unique 'Barking' penalty evolved as a way to add humor and stakes to what is otherwise a simple math/memory game.

setup.players: 3 players is the classic competitive format.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Ace is high, 2 is low.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 3 cards. The rest form a stock pile.

rules.objective: Avoid being the last player left with cards in your hand at the end of Phase Two.
rules.gameplay: Phase 1: All players play one card to each trick; highest rank wins the trick. If there is a tie for highest, the tied players play again until the tie is broken. After each play, players draw from the stock to keep three cards until the stock is empty. The last card of the stock sets the trump suit for Phase 2. When the stock is exhausted, play continues without drawing until the player whose turn it is has no card to play; then Phase 2 begins. Phase 2: The holder of the trump card leads. You must either beat the previous card or sequence (higher same suit or any trump) or pick up the lowest card or sequence from the trick. The last player left with cards loses and is the Dog.
keyRules: Phase 1: All play one card per trick; no follow suit; highest rank wins; ties broken by replay.
Phase 2: Trump from last card of stock; beat by higher same suit or any trump, or pick up lowest card or sequence from trick.
Last player left with cards loses and is called the Dog.

strategy.basic: In Phase 1, try to win tricks with high cards of the same suit. This gives you 'runs' in Phase 2, which are very hard for opponents to beat (they must beat the whole run).
strategy.intermediate: Hand Balancing: Don't win every trick in Phase 1. If you have too many cards in Phase 2, you are more likely to get stuck picking up even more.
strategy.advanced: The Sequence Trap: In Phase 2, if you have a sequence like 8-9-10 of Spades, wait until your opponent plays a low Spade. Then dump the entire sequence on them. They will likely have to pick it up, adding 3 cards to their hand.
tips: Keep track of the Aces during Phase 1. Knowing who has the 'Exit cards' for Phase 2 is vital.
If you are leading in Phase 2, lead your middle-range cards first. Save your Aces for when you need to capture a trick to lead again.

variations.name: Tie: take back and deal
variations.description: When there is a tie for highest card in phase 1, the tied players take their cards back; the other cards in the trick are arranged in ascending order and dealt one at a time to the tied players as evenly as possible, counterclockwise from the last player who played a tied card.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule-only variation; no engine overrides documented.

variations.name: Trump ends trick
variations.description: In phase 2, a trump played on a non-trump immediately ends the trick; the player of the trump sets the cards aside and leads to a new trick.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule-only variation; no engine overrides documented.

variations.name: Pick lowest card only
variations.description: When picking up from a trick, only the lowest card is taken; if the lowest play is a sequence, only the bottom card of that sequence is taken. A sequence counts as in play until all its cards have been removed.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule-only variation; no engine overrides documented.

scoring.winCondition: The last player left with cards in hand loses and is called the Dog; all other players win.
